In 2023, EOG joined OGMP 2.0, a multistakeholder initiative developed by the United Nations Environment Programme and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition. EOG committed to reporting on methane emissions consistent with the OGMP 2.0 Framework, which is a comprehensive measurement-based reporting framework for the oil and gas industry designed to improve transparency of methane emissions reporting. We submitted our OGMP 2.0 implementation plan in May 2024 and achieved Gold Standard Pathway.

Each of EOG's operating areas has an ongoing leak detection and repair (LDAR) program that detects leaks throughout our facilities, including at central tank batteries, compressor stations, and production facilities. While LDAR programs are required for certain EOG locations by state regulations and/or federal regulations, EOG has also implemented a voluntary LDAR program across our operations at facilities that are not otherwise subject to regulatory LDAR requirements and has enhanced its LDAR program in some operating areas by increasing the frequency of surveys. In 2024, we visited approximately 94% of facilities at least twice during the year with leak detection equipment, and the other 6% at least once.

note: criteria 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — 5 of 5. Criterion 1 (quantitative grounding) satisfied: p.6 tear sheet reports methane intensity rate at 0.6 metric tons CO2e/MBoe for 2024 and methane emissions percentage at 0.04% for 2024, alongside wellhead gas capture rate of 99.9%; all figures carry explicit units and a five-year series (2020–2024). Criterion 2 (target-bound) satisfied: p.34 discloses a named near-zero methane emissions target defined as ≤0.20% methane emissions percentage with a target window of 2025–2030 covering U.S. and Trinidad gross operated Scope 1 methane emissions; additionally OGMP 2.0 Gold Standard Pathway was achieved in 2024 per p.29, representing a named framework commitment with a stated reporting level. The methane target does not carry a separate numeric baseline year (as opposed to the GHG intensity target's 2019 base year) — this borderline is noted but does not disqualify criterion 2 because a named target with a defined quantitative threshold and target period is present. Criterion 3 (methodology disclosed) satisfied: p.29 names OGMP 2.0 as a comprehensive measurement-based reporting framework explicitly applied to methane emissions; p.26 describes the LDAR programme methodology including component-level monitoring, OGI technology, proprietary automated LDAR systems (iEnvironmental), and continuous monitoring (iSense); the EPA GHGRP methodology used to calculate methane emissions is stated elsewhere in the Definitions section cross-cutting M1 and O1. Criterion 4 (time horizon) satisfied: 2024 anchor year explicit; near-zero methane target window 2025–2030 stated on p.34. Criterion 5 (progress tracking) satisfied: methane emissions percentage series 0.08 / 0.06 / 0.04 / 0.04 / 0.04 for 2020–2024 and methane intensity rate 0.8 / 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.6 for 2020–2024 provide anchor year plus four prior years — both series visible on p.6 tear sheet and charted on p.32. Boundary call: flaring-related methane content (flaring intensity row on p.6) crosses O1 and O2 boundary per handbook; those figures are included in M1 spans and O2 spans respectively and noted here for cross-concept awareness. assured set false: assurer not named in any selected span (same finding as M1 and M3). OGMP 2.0 note: EOG achieved Gold Standard Pathway per p.29; handbook pitfall warns against crediting OGMP membership without a stated reporting level — Gold Standard is the highest OGMP 2.0 tier and constitutes a named reporting level, satisfying that threshold. Cross-concept notes: methane emissions percentage and intensity rows in span 1 also appear in M1 Scope 1 data; span 3 LDAR programme also informs F1.
